Steelers vs Bengals DraftKings Showdown Picks: Sunday Night Football NFL DFS Captains, Projections and Sim Plays

DraftKings Showdown · Sunday Night Football, November 15 · NFL Week 10 · By Chris Spags · · Numbers as of November 15, 7:10 PM ET

Joe Burrow has the highest SPAGS projection in the Steelers at Bengals DraftKings Showdown: 20.8 points at $10,600 FLEX, 31.2 at captain for $15,900. Across 100,000 simulations Burrow holds 68% of the winning-lineup credit.

Ja'Marr Chase has the largest captain share: 15.3% of the simulated winning-lineup credit comes with Chase at captain. The model gives him 8.9 targets on 34.9 routes. Jaylen Warren is the next captain in line, at 14.6%. The model gives him 12.5 carries and 4.3 targets.

Cincinnati is a 3.5-point favorite, and the implied totals are 26.5 for the Bengals and 23 for the Steelers.

Behind Burrow, Chase and Warren, the next projections are Tee Higgins (16.9, $10,400), Chase Brown (16.6, $8,400) and Aaron Rodgers (16.1, $9,000).

Every projection below is a SPAGS model estimate from the November 15, 7:10 PM ET run of the Splash Play NFL model. Winning-lineup and captain credit come from 100,000 simulations of the Showdown contest, and tied winning entries share credit. A player's simulated floor is his 10th-percentile score and his ceiling is his 95th. Showdown lineups use one captain, who scores 1.5x at 1.5x salary, and five FLEX players.

Chris Spags' latest NFL DFS breakdown on the Splash Play NFL channel.

SNF Showdown captain picks: who the sim wins with

Captain: Ja'Marr Chase, CIN WR ($11,000 FLEX / $16,500 CPT)

Ja'Marr Chase holds 15.3% of the simulated winning-lineup credit as a captain, more than any other player in this game. At captain he costs $16,500 and the 19.8-point SPAGS model projection becomes 29.6 with the 1.5x captain multiplier. The model gives him 8.9 targets on 34.9 routes. Across 100,000 simulations Chase averaged 19.7 points with a simulated floor of 5.9 and a ceiling of 42.9. He holds 51% of the simulated winning-lineup credit: 15.3% as the captain and 36.0% in a FLEX spot.

Captain: Jaylen Warren, PIT RB ($9,600 FLEX / $14,400 CPT)

Jaylen Warren holds 14.6% of the simulated winning-lineup credit as a captain. At captain he costs $14,400 and the 18.1-point SPAGS model projection becomes 27.1 with the 1.5x captain multiplier. The model gives him 12.5 carries and 4.3 targets. Across 100,000 simulations Warren averaged 18.0 points with a simulated floor of 6.0 and a ceiling of 35.2. He holds 54% of the simulated winning-lineup credit: 14.6% as the captain and 39.5% in a FLEX spot.

Captain: Chase Brown, CIN RB ($8,400 FLEX / $12,600 CPT)

Chase Brown holds 13.5% of the simulated winning-lineup credit as a captain. At captain he costs $12,600 and the 16.6-point SPAGS model projection becomes 25.0 with the 1.5x captain multiplier. The model gives him 14.4 carries and 5.3 targets. Across 100,000 simulations Brown averaged 16.6 points with a simulated floor of 5.2 and a ceiling of 34.3. He holds 52% of the simulated winning-lineup credit: 13.5% as the captain and 38.3% in a FLEX spot.

Joe Burrow, CIN QB ($10,600 FLEX / $15,900 CPT)

Across 100,000 simulations Burrow averaged 20.7 points with a simulated floor of 12.0 and a ceiling of 38.8. He holds 68% of the simulated winning-lineup credit: 11.4% as the captain and 56.4% in a FLEX spot.

Tee Higgins, CIN WR ($10,400 FLEX / $15,600 CPT)

Tee Higgins carries the 4th-highest SPAGS model projection in the game at 16.9 DraftKings points for a $10,400 FLEX salary ($15,600 at captain). The model gives him 7.4 targets on 34.6 routes. Across 100,000 simulations Higgins averaged 17.0 points with a simulated floor of 3.8 and a ceiling of 41.8. He holds 39% of the simulated winning-lineup credit: 12.0% as the captain and 27.5% in a FLEX spot.

Aaron Rodgers carries the 6th-highest SPAGS model projection in the game at 16.1 DraftKings points for a $9,000 FLEX salary ($13,500 at captain). Across 100,000 simulations Rodgers averaged 16.1 points with a simulated floor of 9.0 and a ceiling of 29.8. Across 100,000 simulations Metcalf averaged 13.2 points with a simulated floor of 2.3 and a ceiling of 33.3. He holds 35% of the simulated winning-lineup credit: 8.9% as the captain and 26.2% in a FLEX spot.

Across 100,000 simulations Washington averaged 8.4 points with a simulated floor of 0.1 and a ceiling of 23.5. He holds 30% of the simulated winning-lineup credit: 4.0% as the captain and 25.8% in a FLEX spot.

Value: Pat Freiermuth, PIT TE ($4,600 FLEX / $6,900 CPT)

Pat Freiermuth projects for 8.1 DraftKings points at a $4,600 FLEX salary, 1.77 projected points per $1,000. The model gives him 4.7 targets on 24.4 routes. Across 100,000 simulations Freiermuth averaged 8.1 points with a simulated floor of 0.3 and a ceiling of 21.8. Steelers vs Bengals DraftKings Showdown FAQ

Who is the best captain for the Steelers vs Bengals DraftKings Showdown?

Ja'Marr Chase holds the largest captain share of simulated winning lineups at 15.3%, ahead of Jaylen Warren (14.6%) and Chase Brown (13.5%), across 100,000 simulations.

What is the best DraftKings Showdown lineup for Steelers vs Bengals?

Build around Chase Brown at captain with Joe Burrow, Jaylen Warren and Aaron Rodgers at FLEX. That is the core of the lineup that won the most simulations in Chris Spags' pool (188 of 100,000 simulated contests), and it leaves $8,200 for the last two FLEX spots.

Who has the highest projection in Steelers vs Bengals DraftKings Showdown?

Joe Burrow leads the SPAGS model at 20.8 DraftKings points for $10,600 at FLEX, or 31.2 points at captain for $15,900.

What are the DraftKings salaries for Steelers vs Bengals Showdown?

Ja'Marr Chase is the most expensive player at $11,000 FLEX and $16,500 at captain. All 29 players with a SPAGS projection are listed above with FLEX salary, captain salary and projection.

What are the best value plays in Steelers vs Bengals DraftKings Showdown?

At $5,000 and under, the best projected points per $1,000 belong to Darnell Washington (8.4 points at $3,600), Pat Freiermuth (8.1 points at $4,600) and Chris Boswell (8.3 points at $5,000).

What is the Steelers vs Bengals spread and total?

The Bengals are a 3.5-point favorite in a game totaled at 49.5, with implied team totals of 26.5 for the Bengals and 23 for the Steelers.
